issues.description: The solution repository's Person model uses a different attribute name for the person's given name ('givenName' with getGivenName()/setGivenName()) while the problem statement, the template Person model, and other code (PersonScene Table column PropertyValueFactory and PersonService) expect 'firstName' (getFirstName()/setFirstName()). This name mismatch across artifacts will cause compilation/runtime errors and confuses students because the model's property names are inconsistent with the rest of the code and the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Person model's attribute names and accessor methods consistent across all artifacts. E.g., rename 'givenName' to 'firstName' and provide getFirstName()/setFirstName() in src/common/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Person.java in the solution repository, or alternatively update PersonScene, PersonService, and all usages to reference 'givenName' everywhere. Prefer matching the problem statement and the template (use 'firstName') so student-facing code and the spec are coherent.

issues.description: The Person model's first-name attribute is named inconsistently across artifacts: the problem statement and the template code use the field name "firstName" (and corresponding getters/setters), while the solution's Person class uses the identifier "givenName". This breaks the one-to-one mapping students expect between the described Person concept and the implementation (and causes other classes to still reference firstName), creating unnecessary confusion and reflection errors when matching requirements to code.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent identifier for the person's first name across all artifacts. Rename the solution model's field and accessors from "givenName" back to "firstName" (getFirstName/setFirstName), or alternatively rename all references in the template and server/client code to "givenName". Prefer restoring "firstName" to align with the problem statement and template code.
